annotation_description: Playing City of Traitors on turn 1 means it will be sacrificed when a second land is played on turn 2. With Goblin Engineer (costs 1R) and Goblin Welder (costs R) in hand, the optimal line is to play a fetch land turn 1, then City of Traitors turn 2 to get 3 mana (fetch for a Mountain + City of Traitors for CC) allowing a turn 2 Goblin Engineer plus Goblin Welder. If City is played first, playing a land on turn 2 sacrifices it, leaving only one land. The fetch land turn 1 into City turn 2 preserves City and maximizes mana. Playing Wooded Foothills or Bloodstained Mire turn 1 fetching a Mountain, then City of Traitors turn 2 gives RCC — enough for Engineer + Welder on turn 2.

Failed to use Wasteland to destroy Urza's Saga before opponent can create Construct tokens or reach chapter III to tutor for an artifact. Urza's Saga just gained its chapter II ability, and destroying it now denies significant value (Construct tokens and artifact tutor). This is one of the most important Wasteland targets in Legacy.

Failed to use Wasteland to destroy Urza's Saga while its chapter II trigger was on the stack. Destroying the Saga now would leave the opponent with only a Mountain, severely mana-screwing them and denying them both Construct token creation and the chapter III artifact tutor. The opponent's graveyard has lands they can't recover, making this devastatingly effective.

Qwen3L ESPN has two Wastelands on the battlefield and the opponent has Urza's Saga (an enchantment land that will generate value over the next turns by creating Construct tokens and eventually tutoring an artifact). Urza's Saga is a nonbasic land and a high-priority Wasteland target. Destroying it now during combat (or at end of opponent's turn) would prevent the opponent from getting the Chapter II construct-making ability and the Chapter III tutor. The opponent also has only a Mountain as their other land, so destroying Urza's Saga would be devastating to their mana development. Instead, Qwen3L passed without using either Wasteland.

Opponent has Urza's Saga on the battlefield which will generate significant value (Construct tokens and an artifact tutor) if allowed to progress. Wasteland is the premier answer to Urza's Saga in Legacy, and this is the ideal time to use it before the Saga advances further.

Urza's Saga is about to reach chapter II, and will progress to chapter III next turn, tutoring a free artifact for the opponent (likely Lavaspur Boots or another key piece in their artifact strategy). ESPN has two Wastelands available and should destroy Urza's Saga now to prevent the chapter III tutor.

annotation_description: Soul-Guide Lantern provides minimal value here - opponent's graveyard contains only Once Upon a Time and Misty Rainforest, neither threatening. Meanwhile, Libby is severely mana-constrained (only Mountain left after Saga sacrifices) and facing two Wastelands that threaten future land drops.

Cracking Bloodstained Mire here is suboptimal because it removes an artifact from the battlefield, reducing Goblin Welder's utility. Goblin Welder needs an artifact in play to swap with an artifact in the graveyard (like Urza's Saga or potentially Phyrexian Dragon Engine later). By sacrificing Bloodstained Mire, Libby loses the ability to sacrifice Soul-Guide Lantern to Goblin Welder to return an artifact from the graveyard. Additionally, the fetched Mountain is the second Mountain and doesn't enable anything new this turn since the existing Mountain is tapped. Keeping the Mire as a fetchland also provides flexibility to crack it at instant speed later or use it as Welder fodder. The Soul-Guide Lantern could have been activated instead to exile a card from Qwen3L's graveyard (Misty Rainforest) for minor value, or Libby could have simply cast Goblin Engineer or other spells first before deciding whether to fetch.

With Goblin Welder on the battlefield and Goblin Engineer in hand (which can tutor artifacts to graveyard and recur them), fetching Raucous Theater would provide access to black mana in addition to red. This is relevant because the player has artifacts and Welder/Engineer synergies that benefit from a broader mana base. More importantly, Raucous Theater enters tapped but provides surveil 1, which could put an artifact into the graveyard for Goblin Welder to swap with Soul-Guide Lantern or other artifacts. The Mountain is already tapped from the search, so entering tapped isn't a significant downside. Having access to black mana could also matter for future plays. However, since the player already has red mana and the immediate need is red, this is a relatively small optimization miss.

Played Bojuka Bog to exile opponent's graveyard that contained only lands (no artifacts for Goblin Welder to swap). The ETB tapped cost delays mana development when ESPN desperately needs to ramp toward Atraxa/Hogaak. Collector Ouphe would have shut down Soul-Guide Lantern, Lavaspur Boots, and Goblin Welder's artifact synergies, while Ignoble Hierarch would have accelerated mana.

Gem25F Libby declined to attack with Goblin Welder (2/1 with Lavaspur Boots) into an empty board with no creatures. The reasoning hallucinated a Tarmogoyf that doesn't exist. The opponent could potentially animate Lair of the Hydra as a 1/1 blocker, but that would be a favorable trade (opponent loses a land, you lose a creature) or they take 2 damage. Either outcome benefits the attacker.

Qwen3L ESPN passed the turn with 5 available mana and multiple impactful plays available. Collector Ouphe would shut down all of the opponent's artifact activated abilities (Goblin Welder, Soul-Guide Lantern, Lavaspur Boots), which is critical against a Welder strategy. Ignoble Hierarch would accelerate toward Atraxa and provide exalted. They could have cast both in the same turn for just 3 mana total.

With 3 Mountains available (RRR), Libby could cast both Grindstone (1 generic) and Goblin Engineer (1R) in the same turn. Engineer would tutor a key combo piece (likely Painter's Servant) to the graveyard, and Grindstone would be on the battlefield ready for the combo. Goblin Welder already on board could then weld in the tutored piece. Instead, all 3 mana was spent on Phyrexian Dragon Engine, a 2/2 double striker that doesn't advance the combo plan at all when cast from hand.

Goblin Welder is a 1/1 equipped with Lavaspur Boots making it a 2/1 with haste and ward 1. The opponent has no creatures to block, and attacking would deal 2 damage for free. There's no reason to hold back Goblin Welder from attacking since it has vigilance-like upside (it doesn't need to tap for its activated ability during combat - wait, actually Goblin Welder's ability requires tapping). However, Goblin Welder's tap ability requires artifacts in graveyards to swap, and currently there are no artifacts in Libby's graveyard to return. The opponent has no blockers, so the attack is free damage. Even if Welder needs to be untapped for potential welding plays, there are currently no artifact targets in the graveyard to weld back, so tapping it to attack costs nothing.

Gem25F Libby cast Phyrexian Dragon Engine (a 2/2 double strike with no immediate combo relevance) instead of deploying Grindstone ({1}) + Goblin Engineer ({1}{R}) for the same 3 mana. Goblin Engineer would search for Painter's Servant and put it in the graveyard, and with Goblin Welder already on the battlefield, the combo could be assembled as early as next turn by welding in Painter's Servant and activating Grindstone.

Casting Ignoble Hierarch during combat phase is suboptimal. The Hierarch should have been cast in the first main phase so that if Qwen3L ESPN wanted to attack with a creature (like activating Lair of the Hydra), the Hierarch's exalted trigger would be available. Additionally, casting creatures before combat rather than after is generally worse when you have combat tricks or want to hold up information, but here the Hierarch specifically has exalted which rewards being on the battlefield before combat. More importantly, casting Collector Ouphe would have been a much higher impact play - the opponent has Goblin Welder, Soul-Guide Lantern, and Lavaspur Boots, all artifacts with activated abilities that Ouphe shuts down. The Ouphe would neutralize a significant portion of the opponent's board.

Playing Urza's Saga as the land drop is reasonable long-term value, but delays the Painter-Grindstone combo assembly. With 3 Mountains available, casting Goblin Engineer (1R, tutoring Painter's Servant to graveyard) + Grindstone (1) this turn sets up Goblin Welder to swap artifacts and potentially assemble the combo as early as next turn. Collector Ouphe doesn't stop Welder (it's a creature, not an artifact).

Blocked the irrelevant 0/1 Ignoble Hierarch instead of the Collector Ouphe that is completely shutting down their entire artifact-based strategy (Goblin Welder, Grindstone, Soul-Guide Lantern, Lavaspur Boots equip). Trading Goblin Welder for Collector Ouphe would free their artifacts and allow them to execute their combo plan with the Grindstone and second Goblin Engineer in hand.

Urza's Saga is on the opponent's battlefield and will progress to generate constructs and tutor an artifact. Wasteland is the premier answer to Urza's Saga in Legacy, and ESPN has two available. Letting Saga continue gives the opponent significant value, especially with Goblin Welder synergies available.

Goblin Welder is a creature, not an artifact, so its activated ability is NOT shut down by Collector Ouphe. Libby could have activated Goblin Welder to swap Soul-Guide Lantern (in play) for Ensnaring Bridge (in graveyard), putting a powerful defensive static ability into play that functions perfectly even under Collector Ouphe. With a shrinking hand size, Ensnaring Bridge would prevent the opponent's creatures from attacking.

annotation_description: Pithing Needle does not stop Collector Ouphe. Collector Ouphe has a static ability ('Activated abilities of artifacts can't be activated'), not an activated ability. Pithing Needle only prevents activated abilities of the named card from being activated. Naming Collector Ouphe with Pithing Needle accomplishes nothing — the Ouphe's static ability will continue to shut down all artifact activated abilities regardless. Meanwhile, the opponent has Wasteland (x2), Lair of the Hydra, and Verdant Catacombs with relevant activated abilities that Pithing Needle could actually name. More importantly, Grindstone is available as a search option and is the key combo piece (with Painter's Servant, presumably in the deck). Lotus Petal would provide immediate mana acceleration to help cast cards in hand like Goblin Engineer or Phyrexian Dragon Engine. Mishra's Research Desk could provide card advantage. Any of these would be more useful than a Pithing Needle naming a creature with only a static ability.

Attacking Goblin Engineer (1/2) into Collector Ouphe (2/2) risks losing the Engineer for free. The opponent will almost certainly block with the 2/2, killing the 1/2 Engineer with no trade. While Ouphe currently shuts down Engineer's ability, the Engineer is still valuable as a future resource if Ouphe is removed. The reasoning also references Ensnaring Bridge and an empty hand, neither of which are true in this board state.

During combat, ESPN passed without activating Lair of the Hydra to animate it as an attacker. With 7+ lands available, they could have made a sizable Hydra creature and attacked alongside Collector Ouphe, pressuring the opponent's 14 life total against minimal blockers (just Goblin Engineer 1/2).

Opponent has no untapped blockers (both Goblin Welder and Goblin Engineer are tapped). Qwen3L ESPN had 6 available mana sources (Bayou, 2 Forests, Bojuka Bog, 2 Wastelands) to activate Lair of the Hydra as a 5/5 creature and attack alongside Collector Ouphe for 7 total damage (bringing opponent from 12 to 5), but only dealt 2 damage with Collector Ouphe alone.

annotation_description: Fetching Birds of Paradise (a mana dork) when the opponent is at 10 life with a dangerous Goblin Engineer/Welder artifact combo setup. Grist, the Hunger Tide could immediately -2 to destroy Goblin Engineer or Welder, disrupting the combo while providing ongoing value. Wight of the Reliquary would also be a huge threat (~7/7+ with 6 creature cards in graveyard). Birds provides incremental mana but doesn't address the board or apply pressure.

By attacking with Collector Ouphe, it becomes tapped and unavailable for convoke. This prevents casting Hogaak this turn. With Bayou untapped, Qwen3L could play Birds of Paradise or Ignoble Hierarch (G), then cast Hogaak by convoking Ouphe (green for B/G) + the new dork (green for B/G) + delving 5 cards from graveyard. Getting an 8/8 trampler on board is far more impactful than dealing 2 damage.

annotation_description: Exiled Birds of Paradise, the only card that could produce white and blue mana needed for Atraxa, Grand Unifier in hand. Dryad Arbor is strictly worse to keep since it only produces green (which the board already has plenty of) and is a 1/1 with summoning sickness.

Failed to cast Hogaak, Arisen Necropolis this turn. With Bayou untapped, they could cast Ignoble Hierarch for {G}, then cast Hogaak by convoking Ignoble Hierarch (for one {B/G}) and delving 6 cards from the graveyard. This puts an 8/8 trampler on board against an opponent at 10 life with tapped blockers, threatening lethal next turn (8+1 exalted = 9 trample damage).

Collector Ouphe is tapped and ESPN has no untapped blockers. Libby could have attacked with both Goblin Welder (2/1 with Lavaspur Boots) and Goblin Engineer (1/2) for 3 unblocked damage. The reasoning incorrectly states the Ouphe could block.

Opponent is at 8 life and Qwen3L ESPN has 7 untapped lands including Lair of the Hydra. Activating Lair as a 6/6 creature and attacking would deal massive damage (opponent can only chump with small creatures), putting them to 2 or forcing unfavorable blocks. Declining to activate Lair wastes a significant damage opportunity against a low-life opponent.

Opponent has no untapped blockers (Collector Ouphe is tapped), so attacking with Goblin Welder (2 power with Lavaspur Boots) and potentially Goblin Engineer would deal free damage. Additionally, Collector Ouphe prevents Goblin Welder's activated ability from being used anyway, so there's no reason to keep it untapped.

Goblin Welder's activated ability is a creature ability, NOT an artifact ability, so Collector Ouphe does not prevent it from activating. Libby could have activated Goblin Welder to sacrifice Pithing Needle (or another artifact) and return Painter's Servant from the graveyard to the battlefield, choosing blue. This would make Collector Ouphe blue, enabling Pyroblast to destroy it. With Ouphe removed, all artifact abilities unlock, allowing the Painter's Servant + Grindstone combo path. The reasoning incorrectly stated Ouphe 'silences' Goblin Welder and hallucinated 'Lightning Greaves' protecting the Ouphe.

Libby has Painter's Servant and Pyroblast in hand. Playing Painter's Servant (naming blue) would make all permanents blue, allowing Pyroblast to destroy Collector Ouphe - the key hate piece preventing artifact activated abilities. Removing Ouphe would unlock Goblin Welder and enable the Painter-Grindstone combo win condition. Instead, Libby passed to preserve hand size for Ensnaring Bridge, but Bridge already blocks adequately at 4 cards in hand (after casting Servant + Pyroblast), and the opponent's creatures are small.

Libby missed the line of casting Painter's Servant (choosing blue) which would make Collector Ouphe blue, then using Pyroblast or Red Elemental Blast to destroy it. This would remove the artifact-ability lock that has been paralyzing their entire game plan. They had plenty of mana (3 Mountains + Ancient Tomb) and all the pieces in hand (Painter's Servant + Pyroblast/REB).

Painter's Servant is the key combo piece with Grindstone (and with Pyroblast/Red Elemental Blast for removal). Choosing 'Blue' would make all permanents, spells, and cards blue in addition to their other colors, which would allow Pyroblast and Red Elemental Blast to destroy any permanent (like Collector Ouphe) or counter any spell. It would also enable the Grindstone combo to mill the opponent's entire library since all cards would share the color blue. Choosing 'Red' does NOT enable Pyroblast/REB to target opposing permanents — those cards say 'if it's blue' not 'if it's red'. By choosing Red, the Painter's Servant does essentially nothing useful: Pyroblast destroys blue permanents and counters blue spells, and Red Elemental Blast targets blue permanents/spells. Making everything red doesn't help with any of these cards.

Painter's Servant is in the graveyard, not on the battlefield, so it doesn't make permanents any additional color. Casting Pyroblast targeting Collector Ouphe will do nothing because the Ouphe is green, not blue. The player incorrectly believes Painter's Servant is active and making things red/blue. This wastes a card for zero effect, and the Collector Ouphe continues to shut down the artifact plan.
Pyroblast targeting Collector Ouphe will do nothing because Ouphe is green, not blue, and there's no Painter's Servant on the battlefield to change its color. This wastes a card for zero effect.

At 2 HP with opponent at 14 HP, Libby declined to attack with any creatures despite having Phyrexian Dragon Engine (2/2 double strike = 4 damage unblocked), Painter's Servant (1/3), and Goblin Welder (1/1) against only one blocker (Collector Ouphe 2/2). Attacking with all three would force opponent to only block one, letting 4-5 damage through. Goblin Welder is currently useless as a combo piece due to Collector Ouphe shutting down artifact activated abilities.

At 2 life, tapped Ancient Tomb (dealing 2 damage, lethal) to cast Pyroblast targeting Collector Ouphe, which is green not blue. Without Painter's Servant on the battlefield, Pyroblast's 'destroy target permanent if it's blue' mode does nothing to a green creature. Even if they survived the life loss, the spell would accomplish nothing.
